title: DiracX CWL hints, schema version 1.0
description: The dirac: hint vocabulary of DX-ADR-007, as a hints object keyed by class. The map form is canonical: a class then appears at most once, and this schema is plain properties rather than a contains over a discriminated list. The list form CWL also allows is accepted and means the same thing. This version is provisional: DX-ADR-007 lists the schema as an open issue, and the documents in docs/assets/examples are the vocabulary it is kept in step with.

workgraph.title: dirac:Workgraph
workgraph.description: On a top-level Workflow: the workgraph. Every step of it must carry dirac:Transformation.

schema_version.description: The version of this hint vocabulary the document is written against.

type.description: The VO behaviour type, which is what the configuration service resolves defaults against: MCSimulation, Sprucing, Stripping, AnalysisProduction.

target.description: What the workgraph is for: the workgraph's Active hook disables every external feeder once this output holds this many files, so a feeder's request is only an upper bound (DX-ADR-006).

output.description: The id of a workflow output.

files.description: Files in that output that end the workgraph.

output_sandbox.description: Glob patterns whose matches the job wrapper persists to the output sandbox. Sandbox capture is not dataflow: a file matching one of these never travels an edge and never becomes a declared output.

approving.description: The action list the workgraph runs in Approving, once the scout has drained and before it runs in full. This list is also what makes the workgraph scout: it scouts when there is something to judge and a member the position rule leaves running. ManualApproval is the one that waits for a person: it is Failed until someone signs it off (DX-ADR-006).

data_management.description: Replications, removals and archivals: nodes of the graph that runs, without being steps of the document, since CWL dataflow has no notion of copying or removing a file.

id.description: The transformation's name, as an operator will see it.

operation.description: What its parcels ask the data backend to do.

files.description: What it acts on: a step output as step/output, a declared workflow output, or a workflow input with a dirac:Feeder, as when the files staged to a buffer are removed once the consuming step has processed them.

storage.description: Which copy a removal takes, where the file is at several storages.

after.description: Transformations that must have processed a file before this one takes it. A removal against a workgraph input waits for the step that reads the same query, which is a wait pointing backwards and perfectly legal.

initial_state.description: How it starts when the workgraph does, and the one override on the rule that derives this from position in the graph: a member runs during the scout if it is a compute step or an ancestor of one, and is held until the workgraph is approved otherwise. Active puts it in the scout whatever its position; Stopped holds it back until the workgraph is approved; Paused holds it until an operator starts it (DX-ADR-005).

transformation.title: dirac:Transformation
transformation.description: On a step: the transformation it becomes. Every field is optional, so dirac:Transformation: {} is a transformation with everything defaulted, but its presence is required — a bare step is a submission-time error (DX-ADR-007).

driving_input.description: Which of the step's inputs is the pool, where more than one of them drives it. The rest become the packer's join or the partner it looks up.

after.description: Transformations that must have processed an input before this one takes it, such as the staging replication that puts a file on the buffer this step reads.

initial_state.description: How it starts when the workgraph does, and the one override on the rule that derives this from position in the graph: a member runs during the scout if it is a compute step or an ancestor of one, and is held until the workgraph is approved otherwise. Active puts it in the scout whatever its position; Stopped holds it back until the workgraph is approved; Paused holds it until an operator starts it (DX-ADR-005).

output_sandbox.description: Patterns to add to the workgraph's, for this step alone.

requirements_template.description: What its parcels ask of a site: priority, output storage element, and what EstimateResourceUsage writes back once the scout has measured it.

feeder.title: dirac:Feeder
feeder.description: On a workflow input parameter, directly, as an extension field: CWL gives input parameters no hints slot, and the feeder is a property of where the inputs come from rather than of how the job runs. Inputs arriving from outside the workgraph carry one; everything else is a job parameter.

name.description: The feeder plugin: a metadata query, the ancestors of another input, or a generator of seeds.

args.description: The plugin's arguments, which are its own vocabulary: the query, the run range, the events asked for, and the sample it takes during a scout — scouting_events for a seed feeder, scouting_fraction for a catalogue one (DX-ADR-006).

packer.title: the packer
packer.description: How inputs are grouped into parcels: a plugin and its arguments (DX-ADR-006).

name.description: The packer plugin: PerInput, BySize, ByRun, ByGroupSizeRun, AncestorLookup.

args.description: Its arguments. group_size is the one every packer here reads.

workgraphHooks.title: the workgraph's hook bindings
workgraphHooks.description: Resolved from the configuration service against the workgraph's type; what is written here overrides that resolution for this document. A hook returns an operation and records no result, which is what separates it from an action (DX-ADR-006).

ScoutingToApproving.description: Runs while Scouting and decides whether enough has been done, or extends the scout with new feeder arguments. Its args are its own vocabulary, and a hook that climbs a ladder of samples states the stages in the feeder's own unit.

Active.description: Runs while Active and governs the feeders of the members.

transformationHooks.title: a transformation's hook bindings
transformationHooks.description: Resolved from the configuration service against the workgraph's type; what is written here overrides that resolution for this step (DX-ADR-006).

Active.description: Runs while the transformation is Active and returns one operation for it, or none.

HandleFailedInput.description: Decides the fate of each Failed input: Unassigned, Split or Problematic.

actionLists.title: the lifecycle action lists
actionLists.description: A transformation's action lists, one per state that runs one. Three of the four lists of DX-ADR-006 are here; the fourth is the workgraph's approving (DX-ADR-005, DX-ADR-006).

Finalizing.description: Run in Finalizing, once the workgraph drains, upstream members first.

Cleaning.description: Run in Cancelling, after a cancellation.

actions.title: an action list
actions.description: Actions run in order, each recording its own result. Entering the state resets the list's results (DX-ADR-006).

hook.title: a hook binding
hook.description: The hook plugin to run and the arguments it is given. One per extension point, returning an operation rather than a result (DX-ADR-006).

action.title: an action
action.description: One entry of a list: the action plugin and the arguments it is given, in the form a feeder and a packer are named (DX-ADR-006).

job.title: dirac:Job
job.description: On a CommandLineTool or Workflow that is a standalone user job rather than a workgraph.
